unit: Describe daily study routines, discuss learning tools, and share advice for building good study habits while balancing school and family life.
objective: Talk about making time for both studying and family gatherings.

title: Warm-up
subtitle: Family and study time
question: What do you do when relatives visit while you're busy studying?
starters: I try to spend time with my relatives by...
I usually tell my family that I need to...

title: Useful Language (Part 1)
teacher_instructions: Read each word aloud and have the student repeat it.
Read the definition and the example sentence.
Ask the check question to confirm understanding.
Ask the student to make their own sentence using one of the words.

words.definition: having a lot of things to do
words.example: I'm very busy with my homework today.
words.check: Are you usually busy on Monday mornings or Sunday afternoons?

words.definition: time when you do not have to work or study
words.example: In my free time, I like to relax with my family.
words.check: What do you prefer to do in your free time: watch TV or play sports?

title: Useful language (Part 2)
teacher_instructions: Read each word aloud and ask the student to repeat.
Read the definition and the example sentence.
Ask the check question to confirm understanding.
Ask the student to make their own sentence using one of the words.

words.example: I try to finish my homework before the weekend starts.
words.check: What do you usually do on the weekend: study or relax?

words.definition: To go and see someone and spend time with them.
words.example: I want to visit my aunt, but I have a lot of schoolwork.
words.check: Who do you visit more often: your friends or your family?

words.definition: Members of your family, such as aunts, uncles, and cousins.
words.example: My relatives live in another city, so we travel to see them.
words.check: Where do most of your relatives live: in your city or far away?

title: Conversation Builder
goal: Learn how to explain your schedule and plans.

linkers.use: To show a plan or goal.

model:
Tutor: Hey, can you visit our relatives this weekend?
Student: I'd love to go, but I need to study. Actually, I'm pretty busy on Saturday because I have to finish my homework. Let's go on Sunday instead, so I can have some free time later.

your_turn.teacher: Invite the student to visit relatives on Friday evening. Help them use the target phrases to explain why they are busy and suggest a different time.
your_turn.student: I'd love to go, but I need to... Actually, I'm busy because I have to... Let's go on... instead, so I can...

title: Let's practice
teacher_question: Imagine I'm your relative. I want to invite you over for a family visit this weekend, but you're really busy with school. Negotiate a time with me. 'Hi! Are you free to visit the relatives this Saturday morning?'
student_guide: I'm actually busy on Saturday because I have to _____.
I can visit on Sunday instead. That way, I can _____.
I'd really like to come, but I need to _____ first.

title: Real-world scenario
role_a: Student: You're very busy with homework this weekend.
role_b: Tutor: You're a relative who is hosting a big family gathering.
problem: Your relative invites you to a family gathering this weekend, but you're busy with homework.
mission: Explain that you're busy with your homework.
Suggest a different time to visit so you can finish studying.
start: Hi there! We're having a big family gathering this Saturday at 1:00 PM. Would you like to come?

title: Wrap-Up
recap: Vocabulary: busy, free time, weekend, visit, relatives
Language chunks: ...because I have to... / ...so I can... / ...but I need to...
Skill: Talk about making time for both studying and family gatherings.
final_task: Use one of today's chunks to answer this question: Can you visit your relatives this weekend?
challenge: This week, try using English to explain your study schedule and free time to a family member.
